result.source: Restoran Mon Ami, Trg kralja Tomislava 26, Velika Gorica. Primary source: their live online-ordering system at https://mon-ami.skubacz.pl/ (Restaumatic platform, siteId 204190, currency EUR), which is the exact iframe embedded at https://www.monami.hr/online-narucivanje/ — I downloaded the raw HTML (341 KB) and extracted all 66 dish names, all four-language descriptions and all prices verbatim from the `restaurant-menu__dish-name`, `m-item__description` and price nodes. Cross-checked against: monami.hr WordPress REST API (/wp-json/wp/v2/pages, /media — found two official jelovnik PDFs), monami.hr "O nama" and "Kontakt", Gault&Millau Croatia (13.5/20, 2026 review), MICHELIN Guide Croatia listing, Gastronaut.hr restaurant profile, Tjedan restorana, and a detailed 2023 Eat Out Zagreb review with à-la-carte prices. Delivery platforms (Wolt, Glovo, Bolt Food) do NOT list this restaurant — the only Wolt "Mon Ami" is an unrelated Belgrade venue, and the "bolt.png" on monami.hr is an e-scooter ad, not Bolt Food.
result.summary:
Mon Ami is a family-run fish/seafood restaurant on the main square of Velika Gorica, open since 1997, roughly 3 minutes from Zagreb Airport bus terminal. Founded by the Ceronja couple — Božo from the Skradin area, Barbara/Barica a native of Turopolje — the concept was deliberately to marry Mediterranean coast and continental Turopolje on one plate. The son, Bruno Ceronja, now manages it; the kitchen is led by chef Goran Marko Beus. It has been MICHELIN Guide-recommended six-plus consecutive years (Mediterranean Cuisine, €€€, no star/Bib), scores 13.5/20 as a Gault&Millau "Chef's Restaurant" (head sommelier Zlatko Šimac), and has made Croatia's Top 100 restaurants 23 times.

I recovered the COMPLETE current menu with prices — 66 dishes across 11 sections — from their own live ordering system, which mirrors the printed jelovnik and carries Croatian/English/French/German descriptions for each dish. Sections: BEST BUY, Hladna predjela, Topla predjela/tjestenine i rižota, Kruh i umaci, Jela od mesa, Jela od riba, Prilozi, Salate, Slastice, Jela bez glutena, Vegetarijanski obrok.

Key confirmations against the brief: crni rižoto od sipe (€14,80) and dimljene dagnje na rikoli (€14,50) exist and are signatures; biftek u umaku od tartufa exists as "Beefsteak u umaku od tartufa" (€42,00), flagged "posebna ponuda". Fresh wild white fish IS sold by weight — lignje €62,00/kg, škampi €96,00/kg, školjke €63,00/kg. Dedicated gluten-free and vegetarian sections exist. Note: "salata od hobotnice i lignji" is described in prose on their About page and press but does NOT appear as a line item on the current ordering menu.

House specialities beyond food: their own gold-medal extra virgin olive oil from a Skradin grove, and fresh native black Turopolje truffle served daily. Wine list is 60–65 labels, predominantly Croatian; the house wine is their own cuvée of Chardonnay and Graševina from the Pokuplje subregion, Vukomeričke gorice vinogorje.

gaps: WINE LIST: I could NOT obtain the actual 60–65 label list or a single wine price. The wine list is not published anywhere online — not on monami.hr, not in the ordering system (the Restaumatic menu has no drinks/pića/vina section at all), and not on Michelin, Gault&Millau or Gastronaut. Only three specific wines are recoverable, all from press mentions and all WITHOUT prices: the house cuvée (Chardonnay + Graševina, Pokuplje/Vukomeričke gorice), Krauthaker Graševina Mitrovac (by the glass), and Poy sparkling from Mladina, Plešivica. Sources disagree on list size: monami.hr says 60 etiketa, Gastronaut says 65. Anyone needing the list must phone +385 1 6213 333.
NO DRINKS PRICES AT ALL: no soft drinks, coffee, spirits, beer or water prices are published anywhere.

The two official jelovnik PDFs on monami.hr (jelovnik-11.05.2024.b.pdf, 3MB, and jelovnik-12.12.2023.B.pdf) exist and are the printed in-restaurant menu, but I could not extract their text — the PDF content streams are Flate-compressed and no PDF text-extraction tooling (poppler/pdftoppm, python) was available in this environment. These PDFs may well contain the wine list. That is the single highest-value unexplored lead.

'Salata od hobotnice i lignji' (octopus and squid salad) — one of the signature dishes named in the brief — is confirmed as a house speciality in the restaurant's OWN 'O nama' text and repeatedly in press, but it is NOT a line item on the current online-ordering menu and has NO published price.

Rožata, hazelnut/white-chocolate semifreddo, cuttlefish ravioli, Turopolje escalope, olive oil cake, and lobster are all confirmed as served but are absent from the online menu and have no published prices. The à-la-carte restaurant menu is broader than the delivery/takeaway menu.

Fresh wild white fish is sold by weight from a daily display and the per-kg price for individual species (škrpina, brancin, kovač, zubatac, sabljarka) is NOT published — it varies by catch. Only the four standing by-weight items have listed prices (lignje €62/kg, škampi €96/kg, školjke €63/kg).

DELIVERY PLATFORMS: Mon Ami Velika Gorica is not on Wolt, Glovo or Bolt Food. I checked — the 'Mon Ami' on Wolt is an unrelated Belgrade restaurant, and the bolt.png asset on monami.hr is an ad for Bolt e-scooters, not Bolt Food. So no third-party platform menu exists to cross-check prices against.

The Tjedan restorana 2025 page has empty price fields ('Cijena ručka: €' / 'Cijena večere: €') and its menu is only a PDF placeholder — I could not recover the Restaurant Week set-menu courses or prices.

PRICE VOLATILITY WARNING: prices come from the live ordering system as of 27 Sept 2026, but several dishes are flagged 'privremeno nedostupan'. The 2023 review shows meaningful drift (tuna carpaccio €16→€18,50; mussels €12→€14,50; squid €53→€62/kg; scampi €80→€96/kg), so treat all figures as current-but-moving and worth re-verifying before publishing.
I did not access Google Maps' menu tab or the Facebook menu tab directly (both require JS rendering / login); any dishes exclusive to those surfaces are unconfirmed.

Croatian verbatim copy: I have accurate sentences from the site and press, but WebFetch summarised rather than reproduced the 'O nama' page word-for-word in places, so a few of the verbatimCroatian strings are faithful reconstructions of the source phrasing rather than guaranteed character-exact transcriptions. Verify against https://www.monami.hr/o-nama/ before using as literal site copy.
